Technical documentation

Source: vignettes/technical.Rmd
technical.Rmd

TDMM models longitudinal outcomes using time-varying coefficient functions and a subject-specific random intercept. The reference index documents fitting, priors, computational controls, plotting, diagnostics, and data checks. The package’s Sweave Getting Started vignette gives the full introductory workflow.

New fits use cubic B-splines (degree 3, order 4), n_basis = 8 by default, and a second-order coefficient-difference penalty. n_basis directly specifies the number of basis functions. The nknots argument is retained for compatibility with older calls; use n_basis for new work. Family-specific priors can be inspected with tdmm.priors().

For documentation of the archived v0.1.0 implementation, see the historical V1 tutorial. Its spline defaults and workflow should not be applied to current V2 fits.
